5002.en: X_5002 is the point whose tripolar distances in the plane of triangle ABC are proportional to (a, b, c); the actual tripolar distances in case ABC is acute are ka, kb, kc.
no: As a point on the Euler line, X_5002 has Shinagawa coefficients \((1 +k^{2}, -1 - 3k^{2})\).
If the reference triangle ABC is obtuse, then the barycentrics of X_5002 are a nonreal complex numbers. Nevertheless, for all triangles ABC, the midpoint of X_5002 and X_5003 is X_858.

A method for converting from homogeneous tripolar coordinates (henceforth simply "tripolars") to homogeneous barycentrics, found by Peter Moses (March, 2012), depends on finding the point of intersection of the radical axes of radical circles centered at A, B, C. Write the tripolars for a point U as \(u : v : w\), and let \(d_{a}\) = \(b^{2}\) + \(c^{2}\) - \(a^{2}\), \(d_{b}\) = \(c^{2}\) + \(a^{2}\) - \(c^{2}\), \(d_{c}\) = \(a^{2}\) + \(b^{2}\) - \(c^{2}\).
The meaning of k can be stated thus: starting with tripolars \(u : v : w\), the actual tripolar distances are ku, kv, kw. That is, \|UA\| = ku, \|UB\| = kv, \|UC\| = kw.
